title: Admin audit stream garage and evidence fanout
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Build an intermediate "garage" staging tier for admin audit events that performs per-region retention tagging, immutability sealing (WORM metadata), and deterministic evidence fanout to long-term stores. The garage sits between the realtime audit stream (Kafka) and the final archival layer (S3/GCS with immutability envelope). It must support: 1) per-customer and per-region retention metadata, 2) deterministic content-addressed manifests for integrity proofs, 3) atomic fanout to multiple stores (regional primary, legal escrow bucket, and short-term analytics cluster), 4) replay and re-sealing for retention policy changes or legal hold requests. The system should integrate with existing KMS for HSM-stamped hashes and emit attestations consumable by the evidence export tooling.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Garage accepts audit events and attaches region and retention labels within 3s of ingest for 99% of events; 2) Each sealed batch produces a content-addressed manifest (sha256) and a corresponding signed attestation blob stored alongside the manifest; 3) Fanout to primary regional archive, escrow bucket, and analytics cluster succeeds within configurable window and is retry-safe; 4) Evidence export UI can request and retrieve manifests and attestations for a given time range and region; 5) Manual legal hold toggles pause retention expiry and trigger re-seal/re-index flows; 6) Performance test demonstrates <5% tail added latency at P99 for typical traffic profile.
design_notes: We will implement a two-tier approach: ephemeral staging (garage) written to local replicated SSD with MVCC for short-lived retention/rewind, and periodic sealers that create immutable batches. Sealing produces: compressed archive, sha256 manifest, KMS-signed attestation, and entry in ledger index (region, bucket, policy id). For idempotency the garage will use monotonically increasing commit tokens per-customer region and a content-addressed dedupe layer to avoid double-fanout. The garage will provide an administrative replay API and a verify endpoint that checks hashes against escrowed attestations. Key tradeoffs: more writes and compute at staging vs lower cost on archive reads and simpler legal hold operations.
tradeoffs: Option A: Seal per-minute batches -> lower sealing overhead, larger archives. Option B: Seal per-10s -> faster evidence availability but higher overhead. We propose hybrid: adaptive seal windows based on per-customer throughput up to a configurable max batch size. Using content-addressed manifests increases CPU for hashing but simplifies integrity proofs and dedup logic. Choosing cross-region synchronous fanout increases latency; we will fanout asynchronously with at-least-once semantics plus de-dup keys.
tasks: Prototype garage ingestion service (kafka consumer + local MVCC store)
Implement sealer lambda that produces manifest + signed attestation
Integrate KMS HSM signing flow and store attestations in escrow bucket
Fanout worker with idempotent writes to archive and analytics
Add replay API and admin CLI for legal hold/reseal
E2E tests including replay and export retrieval
